topic: Matrix Exponentials: The Secret to System Evolution
target_audience: University students in Linear Algebra or Differential Equations

sections.title: The Growth Analogy: From Scalars to Matrices
lecture_lines: Simple growth follows the equation dx/dt equals rx.
The solution is the familiar exponential function, e to rt.
In systems, matrices replace scalars to describe multi-variable growth.
animations: Create Text 'dx/dt = rx' in #FFFFFF at center.
Transform Text to 'x(t) = x(0)e^{rt}'. Create a Circle (#00FFFF) that scales from radius 1 to 2.
Move equation and circle to left half. Create Text 'd\mathbf{x}/dt = A\mathbf{x}' in #00FFFF on right half.
Create a 2D CoordinateSystem on the right. Add Vector [1, 0] (#FF0000) and Vector [0, 1] (#00FF00).
Animate the CoordinateSystem applying a linear transformation over time t, with the vectors tracing their paths.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Taylor Series Bridge
lecture_lines: Recall the Taylor Series for e to the x.
We can sum powers of matrices just like numbers.
Replace the scalar x with the matrix product At.
Each term involves powers of the matrix A.
This series defines the exponential of a matrix.
animations: Create Text 'e^x = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2!} + \dots' in #FFFFFF. Highlight x in #FFD700.
Replace x with At to show 'e^{At} = I + At + \frac{(At)^2}{2!} + \dots'. Highlight I in #00FFFF.
Show 3 distinct 2x2 Matrix objects (#FFFFFF) vertically stacked, with '+' signs between them, then merge them into a single Matrix labeled 'e^{At}'.

sections.title: The Formal Definition of e^(At)
lecture_lines: The matrix exponential e to At is a power series.
Identity plus At plus higher-order matrix powers.
Time 't' scales the evolution of the system.
Matrix powers warp the space over time.
This transforms initial states into future trajectories.
animations: Create Text 'e^{At} = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(At)^k}{k!}' in #FFFFFF.
Add a ValueTracker-controlled Slider at bottom labeled 't' (#FFFF00).
Create a NumberPlane with vectors i_hat (#FF0000) and j_hat (#00FF00).
As Slider moves, animate the vectors along curved trajectories.
Draw trailing curves behind the vector heads to show the path of evolution.

sections.title: The Computational Shortcut: Diagonalization
lecture_lines: Computing infinite series directly is often difficult.
Diagonalization simplifies the matrix A into P D P-inverse.
The exponential of a diagonal matrix is easy to compute.
Change basis, scale the components, then change back.
This shortcut makes matrix exponentials computationally practical.
animations: Create Text 'A = PDP^{-1}' with P in #FF00FF and D in #FFFF00.
Show the substitution into the series to get 'e^{At} = P e^{Dt} P^{-1}'.
Create a Vector (#FFFFFF) in a NumberPlane.
Animate the Vector rotating/scaling as P^{-1} is applied (aligning to eigenvectors).
Scale the Vector along the axes (diagonal growth), then apply P to rotate back.

sections.title: Geometric Intuition: Rotations and Scaling
lecture_lines: Diagonal matrices result in pure scaling along axes.
Skew-symmetric matrices create continuous rotations in space.
The exponential maps local rates to global transformations.
animations: Show Matrix A = [[1, 0], [0, 0.5]] and a unit Circle (#FFFFFF). Animate Circle stretching into an Ellipse.
Show Matrix A = [[0, -1], [1, 0]] and the unit Circle. Animate a Vector (#00FFFF) on the circle rotating.
Show the Vector's path as a circle, emphasizing that skew-symmetry leads to rotation.

sections.title: Application: Solving Linear Systems
lecture_lines: Systems of linear differential equations use this tool.
The solution is e to At times the initial state.
Matrix exponentials are the fundamental propagators of linear systems.
animations: Create Text 'd\mathbf{x}/dt = A\mathbf{x}' with 'x(0)' in #FFA500.
Create Text 'x(t) = e^{At}x(0)'. Flash the term 'e^{At}' in #00FF00 and label it 'Propagator'.
Create a StreamPlot (vector field) and animate 5 small Dots (#00FFFF) following the streamlines from different starting positions.
